The ending feels entirely natural, purposeful, and earned. Throughout the story, the central theme is the fragile, temporary nature of Arthur and Clara's residency romance—described earlier as an "architectural folly" and a "biosphere" isolated from the realities of their actual lives. The conclusion brings all the story's conflicts and motifs to a satisfying resolution: the dead battery fulfills the opening foreshadowing of the unreliable Volvo, creating one final, isolated "biosphere" inside the fogged-up car. As the dome light finally dies and the rising tide washes away their footprints on the sandbar, the imagery perfectly mirrors the inevitable, quiet end of their brief time together before reality resumes the next day.
